title: Focused Ultrasound and Stomach-Brain Activity in Healthy Adults
official: Design of a Wearable Device Integrating Electrogastrogram and Focused Ultrasound for Studying Gut-brain Interaction
summary:
This study examines whether focused ultrasound applied over the stomach changes stomach and brain electrical activity in healthy adults. Researchers are evaluating an investigational wearable device that combines electrodes for recording stomach electrical activity with a focused ultrasound transducer. The goal is to improve understanding of communication between the stomach and brain.

Each participant completes two study visits, receiving active ultrasound during one visit and sham stimulation during the other. The order is assigned at random. Sham stimulation uses the same device placement without delivering ultrasound. Participants and outcome assessors do not know which condition is being administered.

Each visit includes resting baseline, viewing a virtual reality video, continued viewing during active or sham stimulation, and resting recovery. Sensors record electrical activity from the brain, stomach, and heart. Participants also report nausea and dizziness. No direct medical benefit is expected from participation.

interventions.name: Wearable Electrogastrogram and Focused Ultrasound Stimulation Device

criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Healthy adults aged 18 to 50 years.
* Willing and able to undergo electroencephalography (EEG), electrocardiography (ECG), electrogastrography (EGG), and focused ultrasound (FUS) procedures.

Exclusion Criteria:

* Implanted electronic medical devices, such as pacemakers or neurostimulators.
* Active skin conditions, such as rashes, open wounds, or severe eczema, on the abdominal area where electrodes will be placed.
